summary: Pinned-model drift after control-plane hotpatch causing mixed-version responses across multi-route sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed intermittent mixed-version outputs for long-lived multi-route chat sessions after we applied a control-plane hotpatch (config flag change) in us-east production. Sessions that were pinned to a specific model began receiving responses from an older variant for a subset of requests, causing prompt/response schema mismatches downstream.

Impact:
- Active customers on dedicated clusters experienced degraded model consistency for ~2 hours.
- Affected tenant (FinEdge Analytics) reported production user-facing discrepancies for approximately 3% of requests during the window.
- No elevated error rate (5xx) observed; symptom is incorrect model variant being served despite active pin.

Environment:
- prod - us-east, Dedicated cluster id: ded-9421
- Control-plane deployment: hotpatch config v1.3.7 -> v1.3.8 applied 2026-03-10T02:10:00Z
- Edge-proxy pool: epool-us-east-3, rolling restart concurrent with hotpatch

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer created a long-lived session pinned to redwood/opt-13b-8bit via session token.
2) During control-plane hotpatch rollout, traffic routed through an edge-proxy instance that restarted.
3) Some subsequent requests for the same session were routed to a serving-runtime pod reporting model redwood/opt-6.7b-q4.
4) Responses from that variant surfaced tokenization/format differences leading to downstream failures in customer's post-processing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a pinned session (model pin) on a dedicated tenant; 2) Trigger a control-plane config rollout that updates routing metadata; 3) Concurrently restart an edge-proxy in the same region; 4) Send sequential requests under same session token and observe model id in response headers and output framing.
logs_and_traces:
- Control-plane audit: pin_commit(session=tn-7f3b) -> success at 2026-03-10T02:07:45Z; subsequent pin_update(session=tn-7f3b) -> commit returned 409 (stale-token) at 2026-03-10T02:11:02Z
- Edge-proxy logs: ep-231 restart at 2026-03-10T02:10:58Z; observed 502->200 handoffs for keepalive streams
- Serving runtime trace: request 0x7c21 returned model-id redwood/opt-6.7b-q4 at 2026-03-10T02:11:09Z; session metadata showed pinned_model=redwood/opt-13b-8bit
- Router debug: route-reconcile worker reported "cohort-mismatch" for 12 sessions immediately after hotpatch
comments: 2026-03-10 03:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports mixed outputs; attached sample request/response headers and timestamps. Asked for immediate mitigation options; requested pin enforcement check.

2026-03-10 03:18 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Observed edge-proxy restart during control-plane rollout. Hypothesis: stale routing cache at edge allowed requests to be forwarded to a serving pod that had not yet reconciled pin metadata. Investigating router reconcile logic and pin_commit window.

2026-03-10 05:42 - Elena Cho (Platform): Found relevant router logs showing 'pin_version_mismatch' when reconcile order was: (1) control-plane update, (2) edge-proxy reconnect, (3) serving pod reconcile. Likely race in cache invalidation path. Adding trace-id mapping to reproduce exact sequence.

2026-03-10 09:30 - Support (to Customer): Applied temporary mitigation: enabled strict session-lookup on gateway for FinEdge tenant (force revalidate pin on reconnect). Recommended customer switch to an explicit model pin override as short-term workaround.

2026-03-11 11:12 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced locally by simulating control-plane config flip + edge reconnect. Created a unit test and started a PR with a fix to hold pin-commit until edge-ack of new route metadata: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/9823
2026-03-12 16:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed reduced mismatch after gateway strict-lookup enabled. They requested postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage indicates a race condition between control-plane pin commit propagation and edge-proxy reconnection. When edge reconnect occurs before router finishes reconcile for the pinned cohort, subsequent requests can be forwarded based on stale routing table that references an older model variant. Key signals:
- pin_commit sequence numbers were non-monotonic for affected sessions in audit log.
- Router reconcile worker dropped a reconcile event with 'already-in-flight' and did not re-enqueue immediately.
Hypothesis: control-plane applied config change that flipped a routing tag; edge reconnect caused a fast path that didn't wait for router to confirm cohort migration. This exposes a commit-window bug where pin enforcement can briefly lapse.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: enabled strict session-lookup at gateway for affected tenant (finite scope). Implemented hotfix in control-plane to delay commit completion until edge-ack observed (PR 9823). Deployed canary of hotfix to us-east-1 on 2026-03-12 02:00Z; monitoring shows no recurrence for 24h in canary slice. Follow-ups: (1) add end-to-end test for edge reconnect + pin commit race, (2) update rollout runbook to pause edge restarts during pin-sensitive config flips, (3) schedule postmortem and customer debrief.
